# gilboa.blog

> Data-driven analysis of US inflation, jobs, GDP, and Fed policy.
> Release-day reads with charts, official-source series (BEA, BLS, FRED),
> and reproducible Python. Written by Yoram Gilboa.

Prefer individual post pages over the homepage listing.
Each post states the print in the opening paragraph, names the FRED/BEA/BLS
series, and includes methodology and limitations.

- Site: https://gilboa.blog/
- Author: https://gilboa.blog/about.html
- RSS: https://gilboa.blog/index.xml
- Sitemap: https://gilboa.blog/sitemap.xml
- GitHub: https://github.com/YoramGilboa

## Start here

- [About](https://gilboa.blog/about.html): What the site covers and how the analysis is produced
- [Home](https://gilboa.blog/): Latest posts

## Latest

- [October Prices Rose, but the Annual CPI Comparison Is Missing](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-11-14-october-cpi-ppi-missing-annual/): October CPI rose 0.4 percent and core rose 0.3 percent. There is no official 12-month CPI rate. PPI final demand rose 6.5 percent over the year
- [Payrolls Look Firmer. More Workers Are Short of Hours.](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-11-08-october-payrolls-revised-path/): October payrolls rose 165,000 and prior months were revised up 84,000. Unemployment decreased to 4.1 percent and U-6 rose to 7.9 percent
- [Private Demand Outran the 3.4% GDP Print](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-10-31-what-the-3-4-actually-means/): Real GDP rose 3.4% and private domestic final sales rose 4.9%. September real spending was nearly flat and the saving rate was 3.8%
- [New Claims Are Low, and Payroll Growth Has Stalled](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-10-25-low-claims-stalled-payrolls/): Initial claims were 194,000 in the week ended October 17. September payrolls rose 29,000. Continuing claims were 1.728 million in the week ended October 10
- [Energy Raised September CPI and PPI. Core Stayed Firmer.](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-10-18-september-cpi-ppi-energy-core/): CPI rose 0.6 percent in September, with gasoline more than half of the month. PPI final demand rose 1.3 percent. Core was 0.3 percent on the month and 2.6 percent over the year
- [The Lower Core PCE Path Is a New Ruler](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-10-10-august-pce-q2-third-print/): July core moved from 3.3 to 3.0 percent on a new price ruler; August core is 3.0 percent; Q2 GDP revised from 1.5 to 2.2 percent

## Inflation

- [What Wednesday's PCE has to do after the hike](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-09-26-august-pce-setup-q2-third/): Setup for August PCE, the Q2 GDP third estimate, and the 2026 annual update. July core PCE 3.3 percent; Q2 GDP 1.5 percent
- [August CPI turned up on energy](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-09-12-august-cpi-energy-core-fomc/): Headline CPI +0.4 percent; gasoline +3.9 percent; core +0.3 percent
- [July PCE held at 3.7%](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-08-28-july-pce-jackson-hole/): Headline and core PCE unchanged; real spending flat
- [July CPI and PPI](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-08-14-july-cpi-ppi-dual-mandate/): Soft consumer and producer prints after weak jobs
- [June CPI](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-07-18-june-2026-cpi-energy-reversal-core-persistence/): Energy reversal after ceasefire; core and shelter linger
- [Core persistence](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-07-11-core-inflation-persistence-services-goods-shelter/): Services ex-shelter vs goods vs shelter
- [June PPI](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-07-25-june-ppi-energy-relief-core-goods-pipeline/): Upstream energy relief; core-goods pipeline still firm
- [May CPI energy passthrough](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-06-13-may-2026-cpi-energy-shock-passthrough/): Iran-war energy shock vs core stability

## Labor market

- [September payrolls stalled](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-10-04-september-payrolls-stalled-revision/): Nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000; July and August revised down 60,000 combined
- [August 2026 Jobs +162k: 62% Restaurants & Schools](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-09-06-august-jobs-rebound-composition/): Payroll rebound concentrated in restaurants and schools
- [July 2026 ADP +44k Jobs, 82% in Education & Health](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-08-07-july-adp-payrolls-concentration/): +44k private jobs, 82% in education and health
- [June jobs report](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-07-03-june-jobs-report-soft-labor-market/): Soft payrolls and a labor-force drop
- [June labor dashboard](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-06-27-june-labor-market-resilience-energy-shock/): Headline resilience vs slower hiring flows
- [May jobs](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-06-06-may-2026-jobs-report-stabilization/): Stabilization at +172k

## Fed policy and growth

- [September 2026 FOMC hike](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-09-17-september-fomc-hike-dot-plot/): 25 bp hike to 3.75-4.00 percent; 2026 median dot 4.1 percent
- [July FOMC minutes](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-08-21-fomc-minutes-dual-mandate/): Dissents for a hike if inflation does not cool
- [Q2 2026 GDP 1.5% but Private Demand Hit 3.9%](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-07-30-q2-gdp-june-pce/): GDP +1.5%; private demand +3.9%
- [June 2026 Dot Plot: 40 bp Hawkish Shift](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-06-20-fed-dot-plot-june-2026-hawkish-shift/): 40 bp hawkish shift with rates on hold
- [April FOMC](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-05-01-april-fomc-decision/): Dissents, dots, and the market wedge
- [Q1 GDP revision](https://gilboa.blog/posts/2026-05-29-q1-gdp-revision-consumer-ai/): Consumer pullback vs AI equipment surge
